answer: Plant a walnut of stake behind every identity: an agent locks a small refundable deposit and signs a public record of its history before it may trade. Peers grow a shared atlas of those records, tracing stake, age, and behavior like a vine across the network, so one actor cannot quietly sprout many cheap copies. When two names share one proof or move in lockstep, both deposits are slashed and both are frozen. Each fake then costs fresh stake plus fresh history, while an honest agent pays once and keeps earning.
